name: og-04-mineral-compartments-to-protocells
title: The First Boundary
question: Do mixed-amphiphile organic boundaries enhance persistence without cutting the system off from geochemical energy?
hypothesis: Over a salt/pH/divalent-cation/T window, vesicles form and selectively retain while remaining permeable enough to exploit the external gradient — a non-empty individuality-vs-access region exists.
objective: Introduce mixed amphiphiles + membrane assembly; measure whether organic boundaries enhance persistence without isolating the system.
proposed_mechanisms: G: amphiphiles, mineral pores and protocells

contract.note: bigraph-schema typed ports (_type/_units/bounds) + conservation predicates; the composite built for this study must declare a ProcessContract matching this face (audited via the workbench §Contract panel).

behavior_tests.name: vesicles-form-in-window
behavior_tests.description: Mixed single-chain amphiphiles form viable vesicles in the alkaline / seawater-salt window (the broadened Jordan-2019 stability map).

measure.detail: viable vesicle count in the favorable arm

pass_if.detail: vesicles form (>0) in the mixed-amphiphile window

behavior_tests.name: retention-without-isolation
behavior_tests.description: Compartments retain internal chemistry AND keep external-gradient access — individuality without isolation (retention × access > 0).

pass_if.detail: both retention and access nonzero (a non-empty individuality-vs-access region)

behavior_tests.name: mixed-amphiphile-advantage-over-single
behavior_tests.description: Discriminating (Jordan 2019): at seawater salt the mixed amphiphiles form vesicles where a single fatty acid fails — the mixed-amphiphile tolerance advantage.

pass_if.detail: mixed forms vesicles; single fatty acid does not at the same salt

behavior_tests.name: membrane-transition-robust
behavior_tests.description: Discriminating: extreme salt / acidic pH destroy the membranes — a bounded survival region exists, not an always-on membrane.

measure.detail: favorable vs extreme-salt and acidic controls

pass_if.detail: extreme-salt and acidic controls abolish vesicles (survival region is bounded)

literature_anchors.expectation: Mixed single-chain amphiphiles form vesicles across broader alkaline pH/salinity/divalent/T than single-fatty-acid models
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Met by the coarse-grained Jordan-calibrated protocell — mixed amphiphiles form ~8000 viable vesicles at alkaline vent pH and seawater salt where a single fatty acid forms none, and the (co-surfactant × ionic strength) feasibility map marks a viable region (individuality > 0.1) at 63/256 points.

claim: Mixed single-chain amphiphiles form viable vesicles across the alkaline / seawater-salt window where single fatty acids fail (Jordan 2019), and those compartments retain internal chemistry while staying permeable to the gradient — a non-empty individuality-without-isolation region.
result: Favorable (mixed) forms ~8000 viable vesicles with retention×access ≈ 0.90; single fatty acid and extreme salt/pH controls form none.

findings.statement: Mixed single-chain amphiphiles form viable vesicles at alkaline vent pH and seawater ionic strength, where a single fatty acid does not — reproducing the Jordan-2019 broadening of the pH / salt / divalent stability window.

evidence.observed: mixed viable ~8000; single-fatty-acid viable 0 at 0.35 M salt

findings.explanation: ProtocellAssemblyProcess broadens the pH window + salt/divalent tolerance with the co-surfactant fraction (coarse-grained, Jordan-calibrated).

findings.statement: The viable compartments retain internal chemistry (retention 0.91) while staying permeable to the external gradient (access 1.0) — a non-empty individuality-without-isolation region (product ≈ 0.90), the key requirement for a protocell that does not cut itself off from geochemical energy.
findings.explanation: Selective permeability — low effective permeability to large/charged internal metabolites, higher to small external resources.

findings.statement: Sweeping permeability (via temperature) traces the compartment through THREE regimes on the retention-access plane — too closed (retains but starves; low T), a viable window (individuality + access, peak ret×acc ≈ 0.92 at ~310 K), and too open (leaks; high T) before the membrane destabilizes entirely. Orthogonally, the viable SALT ceiling rises with co-surfactant fraction: the feasibility map marks a viable region (individuality > 0.1) at 63/256 points (~25%) — vesicles survive at seawater salt (0.35 M) and beyond only with enough co-surfactant — the Jordan mixed-amphiphile advantage as a bounded 2-D region, not a single point.

evidence.observed: retention 0.97→0 and access rising to 1.00 then falling to 0 across 285–360 K; feasibility viable (individ>0.1) at 63/256 points, viable salt ceiling rising with mix_fraction

findings.explanation: Temperature sweep → retention-access arc; (mix × ionic strength) sweep → salt-tolerance feasibility map; rendered as the retention-access Decision view.

findings.statement: The parameter sweep exposed that an exact mix_fraction=0.0 is swallowed by process-bigraph's is_empty(Float, 0.0) and refilled with the default (0.4), which would silently turn the single-fatty-acid control into a mixed-amphiphile run. The composite now clamps 0.0 to a negligible 1e-6 and reads mix_fraction via a state input, so the control is honored. (The study runner had already dodged it with 0.001.)
findings.explanation: A sweep axis starting at exactly 0.0 revealed the gotcha; the fix hardens the composite for any caller passing 0.0.

report.title: Mineral compartments to protocells
report.verdict: PASS — mixed amphiphiles form vesicles that retain without isolating; controls bound the survival region
report.main_insight: Mixed single-chain amphiphiles broaden the vesicle stability window to the alkaline / salty vent regime (where single fatty acids fail) and form compartments that retain chemistry while staying permeable to the gradient — individuality without isolation.
report.conclusion: The coarse-grained Jordan-calibrated model shows a non-empty organic-boundary region: mixed amphiphiles form viable, selectively-permeable vesicles at vent conditions. Hands og-05 a bounded, gradient-coupled protocell.
report.caveat: Coarse-grained physico-chemical reproduction calibrated to Jordan 2019 (the study's proposed primary method), not wrapped membrane MD. In-vesicle network persistence (og-02 coupling) is the next increment.

biological_validation.basis: Reproduces the Jordan-2019 mixed-amphiphile window broadening (mixed forms vesicles at salt where single fatty acids fail).

explanatory_gain.basis: Physical chemistry (window + selective permeability) explains both vesicle formation and the retention-without-isolation tradeoff.

limitations: Coarse-grained reproduction calibrated to Jordan 2019; not wrapped membrane MD (OpenMM/LAMMPS out of environment).
In-vesicle network persistence (coupling og-02) is declared as the next increment, not yet run.

resolved_uncertainties: A non-empty individuality-without-isolation region exists — mixed amphiphiles form selectively-permeable vesicles at vent conditions.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether enclosing the og-02 network in the vesicle actually improves its persistence over the open pore.

followup_study_proposals.rationale: Enclose the og-02 rTCA network in the vesicle; compare in-compartment vs well-mixed persistence.
